title: Meal Planning Basics: Eating Well on a Budget

authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: How can I plan meals and eat well on a limited budget?
desired_reader_outcome: Reader has concrete budget-food staples and batch-cooking/shopping strategies.

claims.proposition: The USDA estimates the average American household wastes approximately 30-40% of its food supply.
claims.recommended_action: A commonly cited USDA/food-waste figure; not independently reverified against a primary USDA source this session.

claims.proposition: Specific grocery prices (dried beans $1-2/lb, eggs ~25-30 cents each).
claims.recommended_action: Grocery prices are inherently fast-decaying (classified here under a drug-access-style fast decay class by analogy) and will drift with inflation/market conditions regardless of when verified; flag for periodic refresh rather than one-time sourcing.

disposition_reason: Practically useful, distinct, low-risk content, but the USDA food-waste statistic is uncited and the specific grocery prices will predictably drift out of date and should be revisited on a recurring schedule rather than treated as a one-time fix.
required_research: Verify the USDA food-waste percentage against a primary USDA source.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Refresh specific grocery price figures periodically; consider using ranges or removing exact cents-level prices that will become stale quickly.
